how: Calls specify a common sword build and a later catchphrase extension for members to join.
A bare maintenance acceptance receives thanks and a direction to the coordination chat.
The maintenance call receives a bare acceptance, without establishing obligations for every reader or the behaviour of silent readers.
Urgent help and hypothetical vulnerability do not explicitly establish a judgement that the room has too few hands.
The confirmed location receives an explicit commitment to add pixels, while the earliest deleted call leaves initial recruitment unresolved.
A member supplies the picture and coordinates that another member explicitly joins.
Starting and calling can be combined in one organising post rather than appearing as separately timed actions.
The common representation expands from a sword to a catchphrase and a black border.
Builders report a completed blade and their presence on the canvas.
Anchor coordinates and a shared template orient placement and correction.
Participants distinguish fidelity to a shared template from correcting its known error, with one preferring compliance to repeated pixel disputes.
A template settles placement only when participants accept its correctness or explicitly prefer common compliance despite a disputed error.

statement: Returning a claimed workable decision from a partly unseen coordination venue
how: A public overlap dispute moves to private messages and returns as a reported solution, while the negotiation and collective approval remain unseen.
Recruitment can route willing helpers through an existing chat whose internal decisions remain outside the public record.
One room cannot test global prevalence, and unseen coordination prevents deciding whether its organisation was deliberately constituted.
Personal pixel use and chat recruitment do not establish either automation or its non-use.
Defence is observed without a recorded turn to scripts, bots, or spare accounts.
Members watch for vandalism, guard the finished work, and spend pixels to keep it safe.
Completion is explicitly followed by continuing responsibility to watch and preserve the work.
Participants correct mistaken attribution of hostile alterations and mistaken identities among neighbouring groups.
Effective defence may require distinguishing hostile changes from accepted neighbour work before erasing pixels or blaming a group.
Competing builders bargain over overlap, space below a sword, and preservation of a mutual border.
A participant spares green work because it is harmless, while a neighbouring visitor seeks expansion without damaging the sword.
Restraint can rest on an explicit judgement of harmlessness without a recorded prior border settlement.
Talk about allowed neighbouring space directly concerns preserving the same black boundary maintained by defenders.
Help is offered reciprocally and later credited for preserving neighbouring works, without establishing that every offer was fulfilled.
Permission to use adjacent space receives a direct reply reporting care for the mutual border.
A reply saying it has been maintaining a border supports related cooperation without dating its onset to the preceding permission.
A visitor identifies the room they come from and carries its effort to stop the invasion into the threatened room.
Outside help accompanies defence, but urgency and a visitor's assistance cannot establish shortage of hands as the causal intermediate.
Incoming chat helpers and joint success do not establish a formal coalition or shared cross-room hub.
Joint maintenance does not establish that pressure produced coalition formation.
Permission for adjacent space leaves unresolved whether any work became a guest inside territory governed by another room.
Distinguishing a few people's intentions from ongoing vandalism does not itself dispute authority to bind a room to an agreement.
The recorded border permission and cooperative reply show no ensuing dispute over who may commit the room.
A proposal to avoid the destructive neighbour receives new coordinates and a commitment to build there.
Retrospective loss reports support relocation context without reconstructing a public collective weighing of fighting against moving.
Confirmation of a relocated spot is explicitly answered by a commitment to add pixels there, supplying the missing return from moving to building.
The stated reason for relocation is avoiding destruction rather than a recorded calculation that the room has too few hands.
Fandom speech becomes a proposed canvas inscription, instantiating the candidate's lore range without establishing a national or political identity.
An immediate warning about an alleged attacker does not establish a quarrel predating the canvas.
The coded attack warnings do not identify a pre-existing tie as the reason for selecting a rival.
Fake game news and a fake modification invite recognition, testing, and complaints under April Fools licence.
The calls and chat direction supply no coded host rule or member-imposed boundary around canvas talk.
Calls are recorded without evidence of a subsequent host boundary caused by a flood of canvas posts.
Interim success and final survival generate congratulations and community pride, including from a nonparticipant.
The reported accomplishment is itself the finished thing jointly marked by announcing that they made it.
Members mark the end and recall destruction of the first version.
Celebration and recording can be combined in a final-product statement rather than appearing as separately caused stages.

statement: Becoming interested in a community's game through joint canvas defence
how: A collaborating visitor attributes new game interest to the joint endeavour before the event ends, without establishing purchase or lasting community membership.
A wish to keep working together until the event finishes does not establish a plan for keeping the collective afterward.
An end report and event-limited cooperation supply no demonstrated transition to keeping the temporary effort after closure.
Remembering an original version's destruction is not itself a dispute over cleaning or preserving a post-close version.
An overlapping builder initially insists on continuing after a neighbour asks not to be overwritten, showing intended encroachment rather than a completed raid.
This exchange begins with a request for restraint rather than an attack call, so it cannot establish the model's proposed pattern of refusing attack invitations.
The same edited reply moves from insisting on the competing build to reporting a privately negotiated plan for both pictures.
A mobilisation call and later overlapping build establish sequence without demonstrating that recruitment caused a turn toward attacking another work.
A post-close recollection blames the destructive neighbour for erasing the original before completion.
The attack warning and later loss recollection supply no coded causal link from the call to a continuing rival contest.
